newsitem.title: USA: U.S. growth pegged at 2.1 pct in Q4 -- Phila. Fed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. growth pegged at 2.1 pct in Q4 -- Phila. Fed.

text.p: U.S. economists projected the economy would grow this quarter at a 2.1 percent annual rate, down from the Commerce Department's latest estimate of 2.2 percent for the third quarter, according to 37 experts polled by the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia.
The forecasters in the Philadelphia Fed's "Survey of Professional Forecasters" said U.S. real gross domestic product growth would be 2.3 percent in 1996 on a year-over-year basis.
They projected 2.4 percent growth for the first quarter of 1997, and year-over-year 1997 growth of 2.3 percent.
A recent Reuters survey showed Wall Street economists forecast third-quarter gross domestic product growth would be revised down to a 1.8 percent annual rate.

According to the Philadelphia Fed's survey, the U.S. Consumer Price Index is expected to advance at a 3.0 percent pace in the fourth quarter and at a 3.1 percent rate in the first three months of next year.
Overall, consumer prices are seen up 3.1 percent in 1996 and 3.0 percent in 1997.

The three-month Treasury bill rate is expected to stand, on average, at 5.0 percent in the fourth quarter and 5.2 percent in the first quarter of 1997. Forecasters put the three-month T-bill rate at 5.0 percent for all of 1996 and at 5.2 percent for 1997.

Economists surveyed put the unemployment rate at 5.2 percent in fourth-quarter 1996 and 5.4 percent for 1996 on a year-over-year basis. In addition, they forecast the unemployment rate to be 5.3 percent in first-quarter 1997 and 5.4 percent for 1997 year-over-year.
